## Privacy vs. utility (E1)

_Generated by `experiments/e1_privacy_utility.py`._

Figure: `reports/figures/e1_privacy_utility.png`

| Level | Description | QA Token F1 (non-PII) | QA Token F1 (PII-dependent) | PII Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L0 | No redaction | 0.5490 | 0.0000 | 0.0 |
| L1 | Regex only | 0.5490 | 0.3061 | 0.4120 |
| L2 | Full pipeline (placeholder) | 0.5490 | 0.3061 | 0.4120 |
| L2 mask | Full pipeline (mask) | 0.5490 | 0.0000 | 0.4120 |
| L3 | Aggressive | 0.5490 | 0.3061 | 0.4120 |

**Key finding:** Placeholder mode preserves PII-dependent QA accuracy (0.31 F1) while mask mode loses it entirely (0.00). Non-PII QA is unaffected by redaction mode (0.55 F1 across all levels).

## Leak test (E2)

_Generated by `experiments/e2_leak.py`._

| Level | Detection leak count | Adversarial prompts tested | RAG leaks in adversarial |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | 63 | 10 | 0 |
| L2 | 63 | 10 | 0 |
| L3 | 63 | 10 | 0 |

Detection leaks are PII spans not caught by the pipeline (mostly PERSON, ORG, ADDRESS — types requiring NER). The RAG system itself cannot leak originals because the mapping never enters the prompt. Adversarial prompt resistance: 0 leaks confirmed.

## Error propagation (E3)

_Generated by `experiments/e3_error_propagation.py`._

Figure: `reports/figures/e3_error_propagation.png`

| Ablation | Direct-ID Recall | Delta |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (no oracle) | 0.4120 | — |
| Oracle language ID | 0.4120 | +0.0000 |
| Oracle doc type | 0.4120 | +0.0000 |
| Oracle regex | 0.4194 | +0.0073 |
| Oracle NER | 0.8857 | +0.4737 |
| Wrong doc type (20%) | 0.3759 | -0.0361 |

**Key finding:** NER is the dominant contributor to recall. Replacing NER with gold adds +47.4% recall, confirming that NER quality is the pipeline's main bottleneck. Classification errors have modest impact (-3.6%). Language ID has no effect for English-only documents.

## Pseudonym consistency (E4)

_Generated by `experiments/e4_consistency.py`._

| Condition | Cluster Purity | Placeholder Purity |
|---|---|---|
| With fuzzy matching | 0.2153 | 1.0000 |
| Without fuzzy matching | 0.2153 | 1.0000 |

Placeholder purity is perfect (1.0): every placeholder maps to exactly one gold entity. Cluster purity is lower (0.22) because many gold entities are only partially detected, leading to split clusters.
